chunks.title: CLO 2026 Academic Month: Beyond Virtual, Beyond Imagination — Digital Fashion Teaching Achievement Showcase
chunks.content: # CLO 2026 Academic Month: Beyond Virtual, Beyond Imagination — Digital Fashion Teaching Achievement Showcase This document presents detailed insights into digital fashion education at Hong Kong Design Academy, focusing on CLO 3D fashion design competitions, zero waste projects, collaborations with local designers, advanced fabric simulation, and a structured CLO 3D teaching curriculum. It highlights the integration of 3D technology in fashion design, production processes, and innovative teaching methods. --- ## Introduction to Hong Kong Design Academy's Digital Fashion Initiatives This section introduces Hong Kong Design Academy's involvement in digital fashion and 3D design education, emphasizing their collaboration with CLO and their efforts to showcase student achievements in digital garment creation. - Hong Kong Design Academy, located in Hong Kong, specializes in 3D fashion design education. - Asa leads the 3D fashion design program. - The presentation is divided into three parts: CLO competition, campus projects with local designers, and teaching/recruitment strategies. --- ## CLO 3D Competition in Hong Kong (2022) This section covers the first CLO 3D competition held by Hong Kong Design Academy in 2022, focusing on creative 3D garment design without initial constraints on manufacturing or production. - The competition encouraged students to create 3D dresses from scratch using CLO 3D software. - Ten students' ideas were transformed into 3D animated garments. - The focus was initially on creativity rather than production or manufacturing feasibility. - The competition was supported by a small grant from Hire Three Youths, used to secure materials worth approximately HKD 70,000. --- ## Waste Reduction and Zero Waste Project in 3D Design This section explains efforts to incorporate sustainability and fabric waste reduction into the digital fashion process using CLO 3D. - The school emphasizes minimizing fabric waste by integrating fabric properties and factory-supplied materials into 3D design. - Students use fabric samples from factories to simulate accurate material use in CLO 3D. - The zero waste project encourages design teams to use all fabric efficiently, with no leftover scraps. - Final products and fabric utilization samples are archived and displayed in museum-like settings at the school. --- ## Collaboration with Hong Kong Designers: Kim Yen Project This section details a partnership with Kim Yen, a Hong Kong designer and LVMH semifinalist, focusing on environmental materials and zero waste fashion design. - Environmental fabrics from factories were tested and used in student projects. - Kim Yen designed patterns directly on the fabric. - Students created 3D garments using these patterns, achieving zero fabric waste. - The rectangular fabric samples show complete utilization with no waste. - Completed garments are displayed physically and digitally through animations. - Animations demonstrate a 4D process translating 3D designs into life-size garments, enhancing understanding of fabric-to-garment production. --- ## CLO 3D Teaching Curriculum and Learning Stages This section outlines the structured CLO 3D curriculum, divided into four progressive stages that integrate digital design skills with creativity and AI applications.
chunks.content_description: CLO 2026 Official Academic Monthly Course Review Online! Lecturer Leung Cheuk Wing from Hong Kong Design Institute provides an online explanation of the teaching methods integrating 3D technology and fashion design, along with a showcase of outstanding student works.

chunks.title: CLO 2026 Academic Month: Beyond Virtual, Beyond Imagination — Digital Fashion Teaching Achievement Showcase
chunks.content: - Students created 3D garments using these patterns, achieving zero fabric waste. - The rectangular fabric samples show complete utilization with no waste. - Completed garments are displayed physically and digitally through animations. - Animations demonstrate a 4D process translating 3D designs into life-size garments, enhancing understanding of fabric-to-garment production. --- ## CLO 3D Teaching Curriculum and Learning Stages This section outlines the structured CLO 3D curriculum, divided into four progressive stages that integrate digital design skills with creativity and AI applications. - **Stage 1: Basic CLO Skills** Students learn fundamental CLO tools including sewing simulation, fabric insertion, and pattern creation. - **Stage 2: Part Separation and Fabric Simulation** Focus on designing individual garment parts such as sweaters and jackets. Collaboration with Advanced Stadium provides oxford cloth materials for students to simulate fabric properties like stone washing and puckering. - **Stage 3: Rendering and AI Integration** Students use CLO rendering features to create promotional images. AI tools are used to generate backgrounds, lighting, and accessory integration, improving presentation speed and complexity. Cloud-based AI services are preferred over local GPU-intensive CLO installations for certain tasks. - **Stage 4: AI-Assisted Look Creation** Advanced use of AI to create diverse garment looks and presentations beyond traditional production constraints. - The curriculum includes homework focused on creativity, allowing students to experiment with lighting and styles in CLO 3D regardless of real-world production limitations. --- ## Advanced Fabric Design and Simulation: Oxford Cloth and Syrinsharki APEX Tools This section describes the technical processes involved in designing and simulating advanced fabrics such as oxford cloth, using specialized design tools. - Collaboration with Advanced Stadium provides oxford cloth for practical student projects. - Syrinsharki APEX design software is used to create fabric patterns, colors, and simulations. - Students draft fabric designs in APEX, considering 3D patterns, wool types, and final sewn appearances. - Traditional painting methods complement digital drafting to finalize fabric designs. - Fully Fashioned wool patterns are integrated into the curriculum to teach both traditional and digital fabric design. --- ## Student Projects: From Concept to 3D Prototype and Real Garments This section reviews representative student projects demonstrating the application of CLO 3D in fashion design development and prototyping. - Students start by gathering inspirational images from Google and other sources to develop style boards. - CLO 3D is used to create prototypes, employing features like cloth simulation, draping, and pinning. - Example: A student designed a flying scarf garment, with 3D simulation closely matching the real-life prototype. - Graduates have won awards such as the Young Tailor Award and local championships. - Students produce real samples by printing and sewing based on their 3D designs. - Some projects are entered into local competitions, such as the 4G design contest. --- ## Benefits of CLO 3D Garment Rendering and Digital Prototyping This section explains the advantages of using CLO 3D for garment design visualization and production planning. - CLO 3D allows teachers and students to visualize designs from front, back, and proportion views easily.

chunks.title: CLO 2026 Academic Month: Beyond Virtual, Beyond Imagination — Digital Fashion Teaching Achievement Showcase
chunks.content: - Graduates have won awards such as the Young Tailor Award and local championships. - Students produce real samples by printing and sewing based on their 3D designs. - Some projects are entered into local competitions, such as the 4G design contest. --- ## Benefits of CLO 3D Garment Rendering and Digital Prototyping This section explains the advantages of using CLO 3D for garment design visualization and production planning. - CLO 3D allows teachers and students to visualize designs from front, back, and proportion views easily. - Digital boards provide comprehensive understanding of garment construction. - The software aids in bridging the gap between design ideas and physical garment production. - Rendered boards facilitate communication and improve production efficiency. --- ## CLO Usage in Competitions and Professional Applications This section highlights the broader use of CLO in student competitions and collaboration with professional teams. - CLO is used in various design subjects and competitions including fur design contests. - The Hong Kong team’s full-fledged club uniforms were designed using CLO, showcasing its versatility. - CLO helps students deliver complete and realistic designs for diverse garment types such as sweaters and jackets. --- ## Digital Twin Concept: Connecting 3D Design to Physical Garment Production This section discusses the academy’s goal to integrate digital 3D design with 1D physical garment manufacturing, creating a digital twin. - The digital twin concept links 3D virtual garments with 1D physical fabric and production data. - This integration aims to ensure garments produced match the original digital designs. - Students and faculty have been working on this technology over the past several years. - The approach supports accuracy, sustainability, and efficiency in fashion production. --- # Summary Hong Kong Design Academy’s CLO 3D initiatives combine creative competition, zero waste principles, local designer collaborations, advanced fabric simulation, and a comprehensive teaching curriculum. Their work demonstrates the power of digital tools like CLO 3D and AI to innovate fashion design education and bridge virtual design with real-world garment production through sustainable and efficient methods.
